title: eBay Standard Envelope for Sports Cards: A Practical Packing Guide
excerpt: Learn what eBay’s 24-card maximum really means, why many envelopes safely hold fewer cards, and how to check weight, thickness, flexibility, and protection before shipping.
author: ManCave Sports Cards LLC

body.content: eBay says its Standard Envelope service can accept as many as 24 raw trading cards, but that number is a maximum—not a promise that 24 cards fit every envelope. The finished mailpiece still has to meet weight, thickness, shape, and flexibility rules. A seller who normally fits only eight to fifteen cards may be making the safer choice for the supplies being used.
The correct capacity is determined by the complete package: cards, sleeves, holders, paper, tape, label, and envelope. Count is only one part of the test.

body.text: Why eBay Shows Both 24 and 15 Cards

content.text: lists no more than 24 raw cards per envelope. The same page limits top-loaded shipments to two cards and excludes graded cards.

body.title: The practical interpretation
items: Twenty-four raw cards is the maximum eBay states, not a guaranteed fit.
Fifteen raw cards is the more conservative recommendation on eBay’s sports-card page.
Two top-loaded cards is a separate maximum; 24 cards in top loaders is not allowed.
Use the lowest limit imposed by card count, weight, thickness, rigidity, or unevenness.

body.text: The Finished Envelope Must Pass Every Rule

body.content: eBay currently requires a paper envelope measuring at least 3.5 by 5 inches and no more than 6.125 by 11.5 inches. It must weigh no more than 3 ounces, remain uniformly less than one-quarter inch thick at every point, and not be too rigid. The address must run parallel to the longest side, and the envelope cannot use clasps, strings, buttons, or a plastic outer wrapper.

body.content: This is why card count alone can mislead. Twenty-four unsleeved thin base cards spread evenly may behave differently from eight cards in thick sleeves, a team bag, and stiff cardboard. A single tall stack can create a bump even when its thickest point barely measures under the limit.
The eBay help page currently lists label prices of $0.82 for 1 ounce, $1.11 for 2 ounces, and $1.40 for 3 ounces. Recheck the label screen before promising a shipping price because rates can change.

Eligible items may have a selling price of no more than $20 before tax. Shipping protection is up to $20 for a single-item order and up to $50 for a combined order. A $50 combined-order protection limit does not raise the individual-item eligibility ceiling or relax the envelope rules.

items: Sleeve each card appropriately. Use no more than two top loaders in the entire envelope.
Secure the cards so they cannot slide into one thick corner. Keep the finished piece as even as the chosen envelope allows.
Weigh the sealed, labeled envelope—not just the cards—and purchase the label for the actual ounce tier.
Measure the thickest point with an eBay template or a reliable quarter-inch gauge. The entire envelope must remain below the limit.
Hold the envelope by its ends and confirm that it still bends naturally. If it behaves like a rigid board, use a package service.
Check for obvious lumps, sharp holder edges, loose contents, or a label that interferes with the seal before mailing.

body.content: Test each packing method before using it for customer orders. A configuration that works with ordinary 20-point base cards may fail with Chrome stock, memorabilia cards, multiple semi-rigid holders, or extra cardboard.

Stop when the next card would make the package difficult to seal, visibly uneven, too stiff, too thick, or heavy enough to cross the selected rate. Do not add cards merely because the published maximum has not been reached.

For many sellers, eight to fifteen sleeved raw cards may be a more repeatable working range. That is practical guidance, not a new eBay rule. Your exact number depends on card stock and supplies, and it should be proven with the completed envelope.

content.text: If a combined order no longer passes the envelope test, use a tracked package and account for that cost before offering the promotion. Our
explains why item discounts and shipping economics should be evaluated together.

body.content: The answer to “How many cards fit?” is not automatically 24. eBay permits up to 24 raw cards, while its sports-card guide recommends up to 15, and every shipment must still satisfy the 3-ounce, sub-quarter-inch, uniform, flexible-letter requirements.

Choose a packing method you can reproduce, test the finished envelope, and upgrade to a package whenever protection or machinability becomes uncertain. Saving a small amount on postage is not worth a damaged order, postage due, or a returned envelope.
